query: caveman mode
note: Literal trigger phrase named in the description.

query: talk like a caveman for the rest of this session please
note: "talk like caveman" is an explicit trigger; the session-scoped framing is the normal way users ask for a communication mode.

query: /caveman ultra
note: Slash-command invocation plus an intensity level the skill explicitly supports (lite/full/ultra).

query: be brief
note: "be brief" is a listed trigger phrase for the terse working-output mode.

query: use fewer tokens when you reply to me, I'm paying per million and this is getting expensive
note: "less tokens" / token efficiency requested for the model's own output — the exact auto-trigger condition.

query: We're about 60% through the context window and we're only on step 2 of 9. Can you tighten up how you're writing back to me so we don't run out before the refactor is done?
note: Needs the skill without naming it: context pressure on a long session is precisely what the ~75%-reduction output mode solves.

query: stop writing me essays. short fragments. drop the articles and the pleasantries. i just need the facts.
note: Describes caveman's compressed fragment style verbatim without using the skill's name; informal register.

query: Please operate with maximum token efficiency for the remainder of this task while preserving full technical accuracy.
note: Formal register; "token efficiency" with accuracy preserved is the skill's stated contract.

query: no preamble, no "Great question!", no summary paragraph at the end. minimal output only.
note: Filler-stripping request aimed at the assistant's own responses — caveman's core behavior, phrased as a list of prohibitions.

query: You're running a long agent loop over ~40 files and each status update you print is a wall of prose. Switch to whatever compressed reporting style you have so the loop stays cheap.
note: Cost/verbosity of the agent's own working output across a high-volume loop; user gestures at the mode without naming it.

query: Summarize this 30-page architecture document down to the key decisions.
note: Near-miss: sounds like compression, but it is summarization OF CONTENT, not a change to how the assistant communicates. Caveman is an output mode, not a summarizer.

query: This announcement post reads like a language model wrote it. Can you make it sound like an actual person?
note: Sibling confusion: rewriting prose so it doesn't read AI-generated is humanizer. Caveman would make it read MORE machine-like, not less.

query: Make the intro paragraph of this README shorter — it's three paragraphs and should be one.
note: Near-miss on "shorter": the target is a durable prose artifact a human reads, not the assistant's working output. That's a copy-edit, not a communication mode.

query: Our inference bill doubled. Help me cut input tokens on the API calls — probably prompt caching plus trimming the system prompt.
note: Near-miss on "less tokens": this is engineering the token cost of an application's API traffic, not asking the assistant to speak tersely.

query: Write me a skill that forces terse, low-token responses from the model.
note: Meta-request: authoring a skill that does the thing, not invoking the thing. Terse output is the subject matter, not the requested behavior.

query: Strip the em dashes and the rule-of-three sentences out of this launch email.
note: Named AI-writing tells in a prose artifact. Shares the "remove text" surface with caveman but needs de-AI-ification, not compression.

query: Condense the product requirements into a one-page brief for the review meeting.
note: Producing a shorter human-facing DOCUMENT is co-authoring; caveman never changes deliverables, only the assistant's own chat/working output.

query: Your last few answers were so clipped I couldn't follow the reasoning. Give me more detail and walk through the steps.
note: Inverse request: the user is asking to LEAVE terse mode. Shares every keyword about response verbosity but wants the opposite behavior.

query: This API reference is full of jargon. Rewrite it in plain language a junior dev could follow.
note: Near-miss: "simplify the language" is a readability edit on a document. Caveman simplifies grammar to save tokens, which would make docs worse, not clearer.

query: Our commit messages are 20 lines each and nobody reads them. Set up a template that keeps them tight.
note: Near-miss on brevity: this is a repo convention/tooling change for human-authored commits, not a request for the assistant to compress its own speech.
